name: Volkov-Saito Precision VS-R44 Heritage 'Legacy'
description:
The Volkov-Saito VS-R44 Heritage is a six-shot single-action revolver chambered in .44 Special, featuring a case-hardened steel frame, octagonal barrel, and wooden grips hand-fitted from reclaimed hardwood. The weapon is a deliberate anachronism — a single-action revolver in an age of neural-integrated firearms, produced by a company known for precision engineering, and priced accordingly.

The Legacy requires the shooter to manually cock the hammer before each shot, a firing mechanism that predates Meridian 88 by centuries. This is the point. Volkov-Saito designed the Heritage line for collectors and enthusiasts who appreciate firearms as mechanical art rather than purely functional tools. Every surface is finished by hand, every action is tuned to break like glass, and every unit ships with a certificate of authenticity signed by the gunsmith who assembled it.

The .44 Special chambering provides meaningful stopping power without the punishing recoil of .44 Magnum, making the Legacy shootable enough for recreational use. In practice, most Heritage owners fire theirs at the range on weekends and display them in glass cases the rest of the time. A small number carry them as daily weapons — an eccentricity that Volkov-Saito neither encourages nor discourages.
specifications:
caliber: .44 Special
effective_range: 40 meters
rate_of_fire: Single-action revolver
magazine_capacity: 6 rounds (cylinder)
weight: 1.04 kg
tactical_use: Not a tactical weapon. The single-action mechanism is too slow for defensive engagements against modern threats. The .44 Special round is adequate against unarmored targets but the rate of fire is limited by the need to manually cock the hammer between shots. The weapon's value is aesthetic, collectible, and recreational rather than functional in a combat context.
cultural_context: The Legacy is a love letter to a past that may never have existed — a romanticized vision of simpler times when a firearm was a crafted object rather than a manufactured commodity. In collector circles, Heritage revolvers appreciate in value yearly. Among working professionals, carrying one provokes a mixture of admiration for the commitment and concern for the carrier's judgment.
known_users: Eccentric professionals who carry anachronistic weapons
story_hooks: A Heritage revolver with a provenance that traces back to a founding figure of one of the major corponations is auctioned for an astronomical sum. The buyer is anonymous — and the revolver contains something hidden in the grip that the auction house didn't know about.
A dueling culture emerges among upper-Mid elites using Heritage revolvers — formalized single-action confrontations that technically violate no weapons laws. Until someone dies.
